'''James Alan Bassham''' (November 26, 1922&nbsp;– November 19, 2012) was an American [[scientist]] known for his work on [[photosynthesis]].

== Education and early research ==
He received a [[B.S.]] degree in [[chemistry]] in 1945 from the [[University of California, Berkeley]], earning his [[Ph.D.]] degree from Berkeley in 1949. His graduate studies were on the subject of [[carbon reduction]] during photosynthesis, working with [[Melvin Calvin]] in the Bio-Organic Chemistry Group of the [[Lawrence Radiation Laboratory]] at the University of California.<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1023/A:1024929725022|year=2003|last1=Bassham|first1=James A.|journal=Photosynthesis Research|volume=76|pages=35–52|pmid=16228564|title=Mapping the carbon reduction cycle: A personal retrospective|issue=1–3|s2cid=52854452}}</ref> He discovered, with [[Melvin Calvin]] and [[Andrew Benson]], the [[Calvin-Benson-Bassham cycle]]. He continued his work as Associate [[Executive director|Director]] of this group.

== Scientific career ==
Besides his work on the basic carbon reduction cycle of photosynthesis, Bassham conducted research on the biosynthetic paths leading from the cycle to the [[thermodynamics]] and [[Kinetics (physics)|kinetics]] of the carbon paths and the factors that control the flow of material and energy in this metabolic network. He is coauthor (with [[Melvin Calvin]]) of "The Path of Carbon in Photosynthesis". 

== Death ==
He died on November 19, 2012.<ref>[http://www.tributes.com/show/James-A.-Bassham-94805169 James Bassham's obituary]</ref>
